question: Which ancient Sanskrit treatise, attributed to Bharata Muni, is considered the foundational text of Indian classical dance and is regarded as the 'Fifth Veda'?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Natya Shastra.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Natya Shastra, written by Bharata Muni, is the ancient treatise from which the origin of most Indian classical dance forms can be traced.

 

• It is regarded as the Fifth Veda (5th Veda), believed to have been composed between 200 BCE and 200 CE.

 

• It deals comprehensively with dramaturgy, dance (Nritya), music, aesthetics (Rasa theory) and stagecraft.

 

• Almost every classical dance form of India — Bharatanatyam, Kathak, Odissi, Kuchipudi, Kathakali, Manipuri and Sattriya — traces its theoretical roots to this text.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Natya Shastra introduces the concept of Rasa (aesthetic emotional flavour) and Bhava (the feeling expressed by the performer), which remain central to all classical Indian performing arts.

 

• It also classifies dance into Tandava (vigorous, masculine) and Lasya (graceful, feminine) forms, associated with Lord Shiva and Goddess Parvati respectively.

 

NOTE

 

• Abhinaya Darpana (Option 1): Written by Nandikeshvara, it is a later, more specialised practical manual, particularly important for Bharatanatyam, dealing with hand gestures (mudras) and expressions.

 

• Sangeet Ratnakara (Option 3): Written by Sharangadeva in the 13th century, it is a key treatise of Indian classical music.

 

• Brihaddeshi (Option 4): Written by Matanga Muni (7th-8th century), it contains the first mention of the term 'Raga' and belongs to classical music literature, not dance.

question: The Sangeet Natak Akademi, India's apex body for performing arts, was established in which year and officially recognises how many classical dance forms?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 1952, New Delhi; Eight.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Sangeet Natak Akademi was established in 1952 with its headquarters in New Delhi.

 

• It officially recognises eight classical dance forms of India: Bharatanatyam, Kathak, Kathakali, Kuchipudi, Odissi, Manipuri, Mohiniyattam and Sattriya.

 

• The Ministry of Culture, Government of India, additionally includes Chhau as a ninth classical dance form.

 

• The Sangeet Natak Akademi is India's national academy for music, dance and drama, and confers the prestigious Sangeet Natak Akademi Award (Akademi Ratna and Akademi Puraskar).

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Sattriya was the most recent addition, granted classical status by the Sangeet Natak Akademi only in 2000.

 

• The Akademi also runs premier institutions such as the Kathak Kendra (New Delhi) and coordinates cultural exchange programmes.

 

NOTE

 

• The other year/number combinations are factually incorrect distractors and do not match the Akademi's actual founding year (1952) or its officially recognised list of eight classical dances.

question: Match the following classical dance forms with their principal presiding deity and select the correctly matched pair:
solution_text:
The correct answer is Odissi – Lord Jagannath.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• As per the temple-dance tradition, Bharatanatyam is associated with Lord Shiva, Odissi is associated with Lord Jagannath, and Manipuri is associated with Lord Krishna.

 

• Odissi, the temple dance of Odisha, was traditionally performed by Maharis (female temple dancers) as a ritual dedicated to Lord Jagannath in the Puri Jagannath Temple.

 

• The dance is also deeply connected to the Konark Sun Temple and depicts the theme of Krishna Leela through Odissi music and Mardala percussion.

 

• This deity association is a recurring static-GK linkage tested by SSC, alongside state-wise origin of each classical dance.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Mohiniyattam is actually dedicated to Lord Vishnu (Mohini being his female avatar), not Krishna.

 

• Manipuri dance is based on Ras Leela, dedicated to Krishna and Radha, not Shiva.

 

NOTE

 

• Option 1 is incorrect because Bharatanatyam is dedicated to Lord Shiva, not Vishnu.

 

• Option 3 is incorrect because Manipuri is dedicated to Lord Krishna, not Shiva.

 

• Option 4 is incorrect because Mohiniyattam is dedicated to Lord Vishnu, not Krishna.

question: Bharatanatyam, considered the oldest of India's classical dance forms, originated in the Tanjore district of which state and was originally known by which name?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Tamil Nadu; Sadir Attam.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Bharatanatyam is the oldest classical dance of India, originating in the Tanjore (Thanjavur) district of Tamil Nadu.

 

• It was originally called Sadir Attam and was performed by Devadasis (temple servants) in temples, with the Chidambaram Temple as its main associated temple.

 

• It traces its origin to the Natya Shastra.

 

• During the British Raj, the Anti-Nautch movement led to social stigma and a formal ban in 1910; the dance was revived by E. Krishna Iyer and Rukmini Devi Arundale, who moved it from temples to the global stage.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Rukmini Devi Arundale founded the Kalakshetra Foundation in Chennai and was the first dancer to be nominated to the Rajya Sabha in the field of art.

 

• Bharatanatyam has three regional styles: Vazhuvoor, Pandanallur and Thanjavur styles.

 

NOTE

 

• Mohiniyattam (Option 1) is Kerala's classical dance and was never called Sadir Attam.

 

• Bhama Kalapam (Option 3) is a Kuchipudi text written by Siddhendra Yogi, unrelated to Bharatanatyam's old name.

 

• Gotipua (Option 4) is a young-boys' dance tradition of Odisha, a precursor to Odissi, not Bharatanatyam.

question: The 'Margam', the traditional repertoire structure of a Bharatanatyam recital, includes which sequence of items?
option_1: <style> @font-face { font-family: 'Mangal';src: url('https://appxcontent.kaxa.in/fonts/MANGAL.ttf') format('truetype');} </style>Alarippu, Jatiswaram, Shabdam, Varnam, Padam, Tillana, Shloka/Mangalam
solution_text:
The correct answer is Alarippu, Jatiswaram, Shabdam, Varnam, Padam, Tillana, Shloka/Mangalam.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Margam is the traditional, structured repertoire followed in a Bharatanatyam performance, moving from pure dance to expressive, devotional items.

 

• It progresses in the sequence: Alarippu → Jatiswaram → Shabdam → Varnam → Padam → Tillana → Shloka/Mangalam.

 

• Alarippu is typically the invocatory opening item; Varnam is the centrepiece combining pure dance (Nritta) with expressional dance (Abhinaya); Tillana is a rhythmic, fast-paced closing item.

 

• This structured format distinguishes Bharatanatyam's presentation style from other classical dance forms.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Bharatanatyam is accompanied by Carnatic music and traditionally performed to Tamil, Telugu and Sanskrit lyrics.

 

• Abhinaya (use of Mudras/hand gestures and facial expression to evoke Rasa) is a key feature codified in the Abhinaya Darpana by Nandikeshvara.

 

NOTE

 

• Pallavi, Anupallavi, Charanam (Option 2) is the three-part structure of a Carnatic music composition (Kriti), not the dance repertoire.

 

• Sankirtan, Rasa, Cholom (Option 3) are traditions/styles associated with Manipuri dance.

 

• Chowk, Tribhanga, Bhangi (Option 4) are postures associated with Odissi, not Bharatanatyam's Margam structure.

question: Who among the following is known as the 'first dancer to be nominated to the Rajya Sabha' in the field of art, and also founded the Kalakshetra Foundation in Chennai?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Rukmini Devi Arundale.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Rukmini Devi Arundale was the first dancer to be nominated to the Rajya Sabha (in the field of art).

 

• She founded the Kalakshetra Foundation in Chennai, which played a central role in reviving Bharatanatyam and giving it institutional respectability after the Anti-Nautch stigma of the colonial period.

 

• Along with E. Krishna Iyer, she is credited with moving Bharatanatyam from temple precincts to the modern public stage.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Sonal Mansingh, an exponent of Odissi and Bharatanatyam, is separately noted as the youngest recipient of the Padma Bhushan (1992) and later received the Padma Vibhushan (2003).

 

• Padma Subrahmanyam is credited with developing a new style/technique (Bharatanatyalayam) within Bharatanatyam.

 

NOTE

 

• T. Balasaraswati (Option 1) was a legendary exponent of Bharatanatyam known for her Abhinaya, but she was not the Rajya Sabha nominee or Kalakshetra's founder.

 

• Padma Subrahmanyam (Option 3) is credited with a new stylistic contribution, not the Rajya Sabha nomination.

 

• Sonal Mansingh (Option 4) is known for her Padma awards distinction, not for founding Kalakshetra.

question: The 'Tanjore Quartet', a group of four brothers credited with systematising the Margam of Bharatanatyam under royal patronage, consisted of Chinnaiah, Ponniah, Sivanandam and which other member?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Vadivelu.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Tanjore Quartet — Chinnaiah, Ponniah, Sivanandam and Vadivelu — were court musicians/dance masters (Nattuvanars) associated with systematising the modern Margam (repertoire) of Bharatanatyam under the patronage of the Thanjavur court.

 

• Another important guru associated with the Bharatanatyam tradition is Guru K. Kalyanasundaram Pillai.

 

• The Tanjore Quartet's compositions and choreographic structure remain foundational to the way Bharatanatyam is taught and performed today.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Other notable Bharatanatyam exponents include Yamini Krishnamurthy, Mrinalini Sarabhai, Alarmel Valli, Leela Samson (Sangeet Natak Akademi Award, 2000), Malavika Sarukkai, Vyjayanthimala Bali, Hema Malini and Nataraja Ramakrishna.

 

NOTE

 

• Siddhendra Yogi (Option 2) formalised Kuchipudi, not Bharatanatyam.

 

• Nandikeshvara (Option 3) authored the Abhinaya Darpana, a dance manual, but was not a member of the Tanjore Quartet.

 

• Bharata Muni (Option 4) authored the Natya Shastra, the foundational treatise, unrelated to the Tanjore Quartet.

question: Mohiniyattam, literally the 'Dance of the Enchantress', derives its name from 'Mohini', the female avatar of which deity, to whom the dance form is dedicated?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Lord Vishnu.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Mohiniyattam literally means 'Dance of the Enchantress' and is derived from the word 'Mohini', the female avatar of Lord Vishnu.

 

• The dance form, from Kerala, is dedicated to Lord Vishnu.

 

• It reached its 'Golden Age' in the 19th century under Maharaja Swathi Thirunal of Travancore and was later revived by Vallathol Narayana Menon.

 

• Mohiniyattam is purely Lasya in character, emphasising feminine grace and gentleness.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• The traditional costume is a Kasavu (white or off-white) saree with a gold-threaded border.

 

• Instruments used include the Edakka (pressure drum), Mridangam, Violin and Veena, and it is accompanied by Carnatic music.

 

• Mohiniyattam finds mention in the Sanskrit treatise 'Vyavaharamala'.

 

NOTE

 

• Lord Shiva (Option 1) is the deity associated with Bharatanatyam, and with the Tandava form of dance in general — not Mohiniyattam.

 

• Lord Brahma (Option 2) and Lord Indra (Option 4) have no specific dedicatory association with Mohiniyattam.

question: Under which Travancore ruler did Mohiniyattam reach its 'Golden Age' in the 19th century, and who later revived the dance form after its decline?
option_1: Maharaja Swathi Thirunal; Vallathol Narayana Menon
option_2: Maharaja Swathi Thirunal; Rukmini Devi Arundale
option_4: <style> @font-face { font-family: 'Gopika'; src: url('https://appxcontent.kaxa.in/fonts/Gopika.ttf') format('truetype');} </style>Vallathol Narayana Menon; Gopika Varma
solution_text:
The correct answer is Maharaja Swathi Thirunal; Vallathol Narayana Menon.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Mohiniyattam reached its 'Golden Age' in the 19th century under Maharaja Swathi Thirunal of Travancore, a great patron of art and music.

 

• After a later period of decline, the dance form was revived by Vallathol Narayana Menon, who also founded the Kerala Kalamandalam.

 

• Other notable names associated with Mohiniyattam include Kalamandalam Kalyanikutty Amma, Sunanda Nair, Gopika Varma, Kanak Rele, Jayaprabha Menon, Radha Dutta, Ragini Devi and Shanta Rao.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Kerala Kalamandalam, founded by Vallathol Narayana Menon, is a premier institution for training in Kerala's classical arts, including Mohiniyattam and Kathakali.

 

NOTE

 

• Rukmini Devi Arundale (Options 2 & 3) is associated with reviving Bharatanatyam and founding Kalakshetra, not Mohiniyattam.

 

• Kanak Rele (Option 3) and Gopika Varma (Option 4) are noted Mohiniyattam exponents, but neither founded the Kerala Kalamandalam or presided over its Golden Age.

question:
Which of the following statements about Kathak is/are correct?
1. It derives its name from the Sanskrit word 'Katha', meaning story.
2. It is the only Indian classical dance form traditionally paired with Hindustani classical music.
3. It integrated the Ras Lila of Brajbhoomi during the Mughal period.
Select the correct answer:
option_3: 1 and 2, but not 3 (Ras Lila was integrated in the 15th-16th centuries, before Mughal rule)
solution_text:
The correct answer is 1 and 2 only.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Kathak derives from the Sanskrit word 'Katha' (story); it was originally performed by Kathakars (storytellers) in temples to narrate epics like the Ramayana and Mahabharata. Statement 1 is correct.

 

• Kathak is the only classical dance form traditionally paired with Hindustani classical music. Statement 2 is correct.

 

• The integration of Ras Lila of Brajbhoomi (focusing on the divine love of Radha and Krishna) happened in the 15th and 16th centuries, which was before Kathak's transition to the Mughal court (Darbar); it was during the Mughal period that Kathak shifted from a devotional to an entertainment-focused form, adding chakkars (spins), intricate footwork and Persian-inspired costumes. Statement 3, as worded (attributing the Ras Lila integration to the Mughal period), is therefore incorrect.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Kathak originated in Uttar Pradesh, North India, and is referred to as the classical dance of North India.

 

• It reflects a fusion of Indo-Persian dance elements and flourished under royal patronage in the Mughal and Awadh courts.

 

NOTE

 

• Option 4 is incorrect because it wrongly places the Ras Lila integration within the Mughal-period changes, whereas the notes place the Ras Lila integration in the 15th-16th centuries, distinct from the later Mughal-era court transformation.

question: Which instrument serves as the primary rhythm instrument in a Kathak performance?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Tabla.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• In Kathak, the Tabla is the primary rhythm instrument.

 

• Other instruments accompanying Kathak include the Pakhawaj, Sarangi, Harmonium and Flute.

 

• Kathak is traditionally performed to Hindustani classical music and can be presented both as a solo and in group presentations.

 

• A distinctive element of Kathak is its stylised expression of the Navarasas (nine emotions).

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Kathak declined during the British era and was revived in the 20th century by pioneers such as Lady Leela Sokhey, Kalkaprasad Maharaj and Kumudini Lakhia.

 

NOTE

 

• Mridangam (Option 1) is the principal percussion instrument for Carnatic music/Bharatanatyam.

 

• Chenda (Option 2) is the primary percussion instrument used in Kathakali.

 

• Pung (Option 4) is the barrel-shaped drum central to Manipuri dance.

question: Birju Maharaj, a legendary exponent of Kathak, belonged to which gharana and was related to which fellow Kathak maestro as his father?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Lucknow Gharana; Achhan Maharaj.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Birju Maharaj belonged to the Lucknow Gharana of Kathak.

 

• He was the son of Achhan Maharaj and the nephew of Lachhu Maharaj.

 

• He was a member of the Kalka-Bindadin family tradition, one of the most influential lineages in Kathak.

 

• Other notable Kathak exponents include Shambhu Maharaj, Shovana Narayan, Sukhdev Maharaj, Sitara Devi, Rohini Bhate, Uma Sharma, Roshan Kumari and Maya Rao.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Kathak's gharana system (such as the Lucknow Gharana) reflects distinct stylistic lineages passed down through generations of practitioners, similar to gharanas in Hindustani classical music.

 

NOTE

 

• Sitara Devi (Option 1) was a renowned Kathak dancer but not Birju Maharaj's father.

 

• Bindadin Maharaj (Option 3) was an ancestor within the Kalka-Bindadin lineage, but Birju Maharaj's father was specifically Achhan Maharaj.

 

• Shovana Narayan (Option 4) is a noted Kathak exponent, unrelated to Birju Maharaj's parentage.

question: Odissi, the temple dance of Odisha, is characterised by the 'Tribhanga' posture. What does Tribhanga refer to?
option_1: A two-bend posture at the neck and waist
option_2: A three-bend posture where the body curves at the neck, waist and knee
option_3: A rhythmic footwork pattern performed on a brass plate
option_4: A hand gesture depicting divine blessing
solution_text:
The correct answer is A three-bend posture where the body curves at the neck, waist and knee.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Tribhanga literally means the 'three bend' posture, where the dancer's body curves at the neck, waist and knee — a signature stance of Odissi.

 

• Odissi is the temple dance of Odisha; Maharis (female temple dancers) performed it as a ritual for Lord Jagannath in Puri, while Gotipua (young boys dressed as girls) performed it outside temples.

 

• It declined during the British era and was revived in the 1950s by the 'Trinity of Revival' — Guru Kelucharan Mohapatra, Pankaj Charan Das and Guru Deba Prasad Das.

 

• Odissi music blends elements of both Hindustani and Carnatic music, and its primary percussion instrument is the Mardala.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Odissi is the only Indian classical dance form featured in Michael Jackson's music video 'Black or White'.

 

• It is deeply connected to the Konark Sun Temple and the theme of Krishna Leela.

 

NOTE

 

• Option 3 describes the Tarangam technique of Kuchipudi, not Tribhanga.

 

• Option 4 is a generic description that does not correspond to the specific three-bend meaning of Tribhanga.

question: The 'Trinity of Revival' credited with reviving Odissi in the 1950s after its decline during the British era comprised Guru Kelucharan Mohapatra, Pankaj Charan Das and which other guru?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Guru Deba Prasad Das.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The 'Trinity of Revival' of Odissi comprised Guru Kelucharan Mohapatra, Pankaj Charan Das and Guru Deba Prasad Das.

 

• Their efforts, in the 1950s, restored Odissi's status after it had declined during the colonial period, drawing on the Mahari and Gotipua traditions.

 

• Prominent Odissi exponents include Sanjukta Panigrahi, Sonal Mansingh, Kiran Segal, Sujata Mohapatra, Madhavi Mudgal, Ratikant Mohapatra and Ranjana Gauhar.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Kelucharan Mohapatra is among the most celebrated Odissi gurus, and his daughter-in-law Sujata Mohapatra and son Ratikant Mohapatra continued the tradition.

 

NOTE

 

• Guru Bipin Singh (Option 2) is a noted exponent/guru of Manipuri dance, not Odissi.

 

• Vallathol Narayana Menon (Option 3) revived Mohiniyattam and founded Kerala Kalamandalam.

 

• Siddhendra Yogi (Option 4) formalised Kuchipudi, unrelated to Odissi's revival.

question: Manipuri dance, also known as 'Jagoi', is predominantly based on which theme, and which eminent literary figure played a pivotal role in its modern revival?
option_2: Ras Leela depicting Krishna and Radha; Rabindranath Tagore
solution_text:
The correct answer is Ras Leela depicting Krishna and Radha; Rabindranath Tagore.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Manipuri dance, also called Jagoi, is a classical dance form from Manipur based on Ras Leela, depicting the stories of Krishna and Radha.

 

• Rabindranath Tagore played a pivotal role in its modern revival, introducing Manipuri dance at Visva Bharati University.

 

• The Pung (barrel-shaped drum) is described as the 'soul of the performance'.

 

• Manipuri has two main traditions — Sankirtan and Rasa — and styles including Jagoi and Cholom.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Jawaharlal Nehru Manipuri Dance Academy, Imphal, was established in 1954.

 

• Manipuri is prominently performed on devotional themes and during festivals such as Holi.

 

• Guru Bipin Singh and Guru Amubi Singh are important gurus associated with the tradition, and the Jhaveri Sisters (Darshana, Nayana, Swarna, Ranjana) are noted exponents.

 

NOTE

 

• Uday Shankar (Option 1) was a pioneering figure of modern Indian dance broadly, but the specific revival of Manipuri is credited to Tagore.

 

• Vallathol Narayana Menon (Option 3) is linked with Mohiniyattam's revival, not Manipuri.

 

• Kelucharan Mohapatra (Option 4) is an Odissi guru, unrelated to Manipuri.

question: In Manipuri dance, which instrument is described as the 'soul of the performance', and what are the names of its two main performance traditions?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Pung; Sankirtan and Rasa.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• In Manipuri dance, the Pung, a barrel-shaped drum, is described as the 'soul of the performance'.

 

• The dance has two main traditions — Sankirtan and Rasa — and its principal styles include Jagoi and Cholom.

 

• Manipuri's predominant theme is devotion and divine love, drawn from the Ras Leela of Radha and Krishna.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Jawaharlal Nehru Manipuri Dance Academy in Imphal (established 1954) is a key institution for training in this dance form.

 

NOTE

 

• Mardala (Option 1) is the primary percussion of Odissi, not Manipuri.

 

• Chenda (Option 3) is the primary percussion of Kathakali; 'Kalasham' and 'Thekkan' are Kathakali-related terms.

 

• Edakka (Option 4) is an instrument of Mohiniyattam; 'Lasya and Tandava' are generic dance-mode classifications from the Natya Shastra, not Manipuri's specific traditions.

question: Kuchipudi, a classical dance form named after a village in Andhra Pradesh's Krishna district, was formalised into its modern style by which saint, who also authored the text 'Bhama Kalapam'?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Siddhendra Yogi.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Kuchipudi originates from Kuchipudi village in the Krishna district of Andhra Pradesh and traces its roots to the Natya Shastra and the village's ancient Brahmin community.

 

• The saint Siddhendra Yogi formalised the modern Kuchipudi style and authored 'Bhama Kalapam' in the 17th century, based on stories of Krishna and Satyabhama.

 

• Kuchipudi received support from the Vijayanagar Empire and combines storytelling, dialogue, dance, mime and acting, and is associated with the Bhagavata Mela tradition.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• The signature technique of Kuchipudi is Tarangam, in which the dancer performs intricate footwork while balancing on the rim of a brass plate.

 

• The Kuchipudi Art Academy, Madras, established in 1963, is a key institution for the dance form.

 

• Noted exponents include Yamini Krishnamurthy, Radha Reddy, Raja Reddy, Vempati Chinna Satyam and Swapna Sundari.

 

NOTE

 

• Nandikeshvara (Option 1) wrote the Abhinaya Darpana, a Bharatanatyam-related manual.

 

• Bharata Muni (Option 2) wrote the Natya Shastra, the general foundational text, not specifically Bhama Kalapam.

 

• Mahapurush Sankaradeva (Option 4) founded the Sattriya dance tradition of Assam.

question: 'Tarangam', a signature technique in which a dancer performs intricate footwork while balancing on the rim of a brass plate, is characteristic of which classical dance form?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Kuchipudi.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Tarangam (meaning 'waves') is a distinctive signature technique of Kuchipudi, in which the dancer performs complex footwork while balancing on the rim of a brass plate.

 

• Kuchipudi integrates dance, mime and acting, and is closely associated with the Bhagavata Mela tradition of Andhra Pradesh.

 

• It is based primarily on the stories of Krishna and Satyabhama, and its formalisation is credited to Siddhendra Yogi.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Kuchipudi Art Academy, Madras (1963), has played an important role in institutionalising the training of this dance form.

 

NOTE

 

• Kathakali (Option 1) is known for elaborate masks and Kalasham sequences, not the Tarangam brass-plate technique.

 

• Sattriya (Option 3) is Assam's classical dance based on Sankaradeva's teachings, unrelated to Tarangam.

 

• Mohiniyattam (Option 4) is characterised by Lasya (graceful, feminine movement), not brass-plate dancing.

question: Kathakali, the classical dance-drama of Kerala, derives its name from which two words, and which instrument creates its primary rhythmic base?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 'Katha' (story) and 'Kali' (performance); Chenda.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Kathakali originates in Kerala; its name is derived from 'Katha' (story) and 'Kali' (performance).

 

• The Chenda is primarily used to create the rhythmic base for a Kathakali performance.

 

• Its dramatic stories are mainly drawn from Indian epics — the Ramayana, Mahabharata and Puranas.

 

• It was traditionally performed only by male actors, featuring elaborate makeup and masks, Kalasham (technical dance sequences) and silent acting with no spoken dialogue.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Kathakali symbolically represents the element Ether (Akash).

 

• Notable exponents/gurus include Mrinalini Sarabhai, Gopinath, Kunju Kurup, Vallathol Narayana Menon and Uday Shankar.

 

NOTE

 

• 'Sadir' and 'Attam' (Option 3) are not the roots of the name Kathakali; 'Sadir Attam' was in fact the old name for Bharatanatyam.

 

• Mridangam, Tabla and Pung (Options 2-4) are instruments of other dance forms (Bharatanatyam/Kathak/Manipuri respectively), not the Chenda used in Kathakali.

question: Which of the following is NOT a characteristic feature of a traditional Kathakali performance?
option_3: Live spoken dialogue delivered by the performers on stage
option_4: Traditionally performed only by male actors
solution_text:
The correct answer is Live spoken dialogue delivered by the performers on stage.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Kathakali is known for silent acting, meaning performers do not speak dialogue on stage; the narrative is conveyed through hand gestures (mudras), facial expressions and body movements, while vocalists sing the story off-stage.

 

• Key features of Kathakali include elaborate makeup and costumes, Kalasham (technical dance interludes), masked performances, and traditionally being performed only by male actors.

 

• Its dramatic content is drawn from Indian epics such as the Ramayana and Mahabharata, and the Chenda provides its rhythmic base.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Kathakali symbolically represents the element Ether (Akash) among the classical dance forms.

 

NOTE

 

• Options 1, 2 and 4 are all genuine, well-documented features of Kathakali and are therefore not the correct choice for this 'NOT a feature' question.

question: Sattriya, recognised as India's classical dance in the year 2000 by the Sangeet Natak Akademi, was founded in the 15th century by which Vaishnavite saint-reformer of Assam?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Mahapurush Sankaradeva.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Sattriya was created by Mahapurush Shankardev (Sankaradeva) in the 15th century and is primarily based on the life of Lord Krishna.

 

• It was recognised as a classical dance in 2000 by the Sangeet Natak Akademi, making it the most recently added classical dance form.

 

• It features both Lasya (feminine, graceful) and Tandava (masculine) elements and is traditionally performed in Satras (Vaishnav monasteries).

 

• Borgeet — devotional songs composed by Sankaradeva and Madhavadeva — accompanies the dance.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Madhavdev, Sankaradeva's chief disciple, co-composed the Borgeet tradition.

 

• Other associated names include Jatin Goswami, Ghanakanta Bora, Ramkrishna Talukdar and Bhupen Hazarika (noted for his broader contribution to Assamese culture).

 

NOTE

 

• Madhavdev (Option 1) was Sankaradeva's chief disciple and co-composer of Borgeet, but the founder of Sattriya was Sankaradeva himself.

 

• Bhupen Hazarika (Option 3) is a celebrated figure in Assamese culture generally, not the founder of Sattriya.

 

• Jatin Goswami (Option 4) is a modern exponent associated with Sattriya, not its founder.

question: Sattriya dance is traditionally performed in which venues, and which devotional song tradition, composed by Sankaradeva and Madhavadeva, accompanies it?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Satras (Vaishnav monasteries); Borgeet.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Sattriya is traditionally performed in Satras, the Vaishnav monasteries of Assam established under the Bhakti movement led by Sankaradeva.

 

• It is accompanied by Borgeet, devotional songs composed by Sankaradeva and Madhavadeva.

 

• The dance form is a style with a specific grammar and expressive facial gestures, based on the life of Lord Krishna.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Sattriya was granted classical dance status by the Sangeet Natak Akademi in 2000, the most recent of the eight recognised classical dances.

 

NOTE

 

• Puri temples (Option 1) are associated with Odissi (Maharis), not Sattriya.

 

• Thumri (Option 3) is a light-classical vocal genre of Hindustani music, unrelated to Sattriya's accompaniment.

 

• Dhrupad (Option 4) is the oldest form of Hindustani classical vocal music, not Sattriya's musical accompaniment (which is Borgeet).

question: Chhau, a semi-classical dance form of eastern India inscribed on the UNESCO Representative List of the Intangible Cultural Heritage of Humanity in 2010, is recognised by the Ministry of Culture as the classical dance form of India in addition to the eight recognised by the Sangeet Natak Akademi. What number/position is it given?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Ninth.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Chhau is a semi-classical dance form from eastern India. While the Sangeet Natak Akademi officially recognises eight classical dance forms, the Ministry of Culture recognises Chhau as the ninth classical dance of India.

 

• In 2010, Chhau was inscribed on the UNESCO Representative List of the Intangible Cultural Heritage of Humanity.

 

• Chhau has three distinct regional styles: Seraikella Chhau (Jharkhand), Purulia Chhau (West Bengal) and Mayurbhanj Chhau (Odisha).

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Chhau performances typically use masks (except in the Mayurbhanj style) and combine martial art movements, acrobatics and folk themes with elements of classical dance.

 

NOTE

 

• Options 1, 2 and 3 do not match the correct sequence — Chhau is specifically termed the ninth classical dance by the Ministry of Culture, distinct from the Akademi's list of eight.

question: The three regional styles of the Chhau dance are the Seraikella Chhau, Purulia Chhau and Mayurbhanj Chhau, associated respectively with which states?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Jharkhand, West Bengal and Odisha.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The three regional styles of Chhau are: Seraikella Chhau – Jharkhand, Purulia Chhau – West Bengal, and Mayurbhanj Chhau – Odisha.

 

• Chhau is recognised as the ninth classical dance form by the Ministry of Culture and was inscribed on the UNESCO Intangible Cultural Heritage list in 2010.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Among the three styles, the Mayurbhanj Chhau of Odisha is distinctive for being performed without masks, unlike the Seraikella and Purulia styles.

 

NOTE

 

• Options 2, 3 and 4 incorrectly rearrange or substitute the state-style pairings; only Option 1 lists the correct state for each named style.

question: Which of the following classical languages of India, granted 'Classical Language' status by the Government, was the FIRST to receive this recognition, in 2004?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Tamil.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Tamil was the first language to be granted 'Classical Language' status by the Government of India, in 2004.

 

• It was followed by Sanskrit (2005), Telugu and Kannada (2008), Malayalam (2013), Odia (2014), and in 2024, Marathi, Pali, Prakrit, Assamese and Bengali were added.

 

• This recognition is closely linked to the broader static-GK theme of classical arts and culture, as several classical dance forms (Bharatanatyam-Tamil, Kuchipudi-Telugu) are performed in these classical languages.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• As of the latest additions in 2024, India has 11 languages with Classical Language status: Tamil, Sanskrit, Telugu, Kannada, Malayalam, Odia, Marathi, Pali, Prakrit, Assamese and Bengali.

 

NOTE

 

• Sanskrit (Option 1) received the status in 2005, a year after Tamil.

 

• Telugu (Option 2) and Kannada (Option 4) both received the status in 2008, well after Tamil.
